parts.label: (a)
parts.stem:
Nitrogen monoxide, $\text{NO}$, reacts with ozone, $\text{O}_3$.

$$\text{NO(g)} + \text{O}_3\text{(g)} \rightarrow \text{NO}_2\text{(g)} + \text{O}_2\text{(g)}$$

This reaction is first order with respect to both $\text{NO}$ and $\text{O}_3$. At $298\text{ K}$, the rate constant $k = 11\,500\text{ mol}^{-1}\text{dm}^3\text{s}^{-1}$.

parts.label: (a)(i)
parts.text: Complete the rate equation for this reaction.

parts.label: (a)(ii)
parts.text:
A reaction is carried out in which the initial concentrations of $\text{NO}$ and $\text{O}_3$ are both $1.20 \times 10^{-6}\text{ mol dm}^{-3}$.

Calculate the initial rate of the reaction. State its units.

parts.label: (a)(iii)
parts.text:
The reaction described in (a)(ii) is monitored over a period of time.

Predict whether or not the graph of $[\text{NO}]$ against time, under these conditions, shows that the reaction has a constant half-life. Explain your answer.

parts.label: (b)
parts.stem:
Nitrous oxide, $\text{N}_2\text{O}$, decomposes into its elements.

$$2\text{N}_2\text{O(g)} \rightarrow 2\text{N}_2\text{(g)} + \text{O}_2\text{(g)}$$

At a high temperature, a small amount of platinum wire is added to a large amount of nitrous oxide. The reaction follows zero order kinetics. The platinum wire behaves as a catalyst.

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.text:
Sketch a graph, on the axes below, of reaction rate against time for the catalysed decomposition of $\text{N}_2\text{O}$ under these conditions.

{{figure:pdf_visual_01.png}}

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.text:
Sketch a graph, on the axes below, of $[\text{N}_2\text{O}]$ against time for this reaction.

{{figure:pdf_visual_02.png}}

parts.label: (b)(iii)
parts.text:
Platinum behaves as a heterogeneous catalyst in this reaction.

Describe the mode of action of a heterogeneous catalyst.

parts.label: (b)(iv)
parts.text: Suggest a reason why this reaction has zero order kinetics when the amount of nitrous oxide is large and the amount of platinum is small.
